headline: 8 workers killed by toxic gas at Sitakunda shipbreaking yard
summary: A probe committee will be formed to investigate the tragedy in Chattogram, as the army works to bring the situation under control.
details: Eight workers were killed after suspected exposure to toxic gas at a shipbreaking yard in Sitakunda, Chattogram.
Finance Minister Amir Khosru Mahmud Chowdhury announced that a probe committee will be formed to investigate the incident and determine the cause of the deaths.
The minister visited an injured worker undergoing treatment at Chattogram Medical College Hospital on Friday afternoon.
He stated that the gas exposure created a difficult situation to manage, and the Bangladesh Army is currently working to bring the area under control.
Further actions will be taken based on the findings of the investigation committee.
caption:
8 workers dead after toxic gas exposure at a Sitakunda shipyard. The army has been deployed to manage the scene.

Eight workers were killed after suspected exposure to toxic gas at a shipbreaking yard in Sitakunda, Chattogram.

Finance Minister Amir Khosru Mahmud Chowdhury announced that a probe committee will be formed to investigate the incident and determine the cause of the deaths.

The minister visited an injured worker undergoing treatment at Chattogram Medical College Hospital on Friday afternoon.

He stated that the gas exposure created a difficult situation to manage, and the Bangladesh Army is currently working to bring the area under control.

Further actions will be taken based on the findings of the investigation committee.

headline_marked: 153-run lead: [[Bangladesh strengthen grip on Australia]] in Darwin Test
headline: 153-run lead: Bangladesh strengthen grip on Australia in Darwin Test
summary: Tanzid Hasan's historic first Test century and a dominant Day 2 performance leave Australia under immense pressure.
details: Bangladesh ended Day 2 of the historic Darwin Test with a commanding 153-run lead, finishing at 351 for 6. This marks their second-best total in 13 Test innings against Australia.
The highlight of the day was Tanzid Hasan's first Test century. The 25-year-old opener batted patiently for over five hours, scoring a century from 197 balls with eight fours and a six.
Bangladesh's dominance was built on key partnerships, including a 102-run stand with Mominul Haque and a 93-run partnership with captain Najmul Hossain Shanto.
Australia's fightback with the second new ball saw three wickets fall in quick succession, but Mehidy Hasan Miraz (32*) and Hasan Mahmud (13*) remained unbeaten at stumps.
Former Australia captain Ricky Ponting noted that the Australian dressing room would be 'nervous' as the pressure is now firmly on their batters to avoid a major upset.
The match continues on Saturday on a pitch that appears to be becoming easier for batting, with Bangladesh firmly in the driver's seat.
caption:
A historic century and a 153-run lead! Bangladesh has Australia on the ropes in Darwin.

Bangladesh ended Day 2 of the historic Darwin Test with a commanding 153-run lead, finishing at 351 for 6. This marks their second-best total in 13 Test innings against Australia.

The highlight of the day was Tanzid Hasan's first Test century. The 25-year-old opener batted patiently for over five hours, scoring a century from 197 balls with eight fours and a six.

Bangladesh's dominance was built on key partnerships, including a 102-run stand with Mominul Haque and a 93-run partnership with captain Najmul Hossain Shanto.

Australia's fightback with the second new ball saw three wickets fall in quick succession, but Mehidy Hasan Miraz (32*) and Hasan Mahmud (13*) remained unbeaten at stumps.

Former Australia captain Ricky Ponting noted that the Australian dressing room would be 'nervous' as the pressure is now firmly on their batters to avoid a major upset.

The match continues on Saturday on a pitch that appears to be becoming easier for batting, with Bangladesh firmly in the driver's seat.
